transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-06
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Sam Lee (CTO, Cedar Streams), Priya Das (ML Engineer), Jordan Kim (Security), Evan Holt (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be incomplete):
- Customer evaluating exit from current hosted provider into a hybrid of Redwood Dedicated and Private for latency-sensitive features and cost control.
- Key concerns: vLLM/TGI compatibility, eval parity vs OpenAI outputs, KMS and audit logs, latency targets (p50 ~ 80ms token?), cost per million tokens target.
- Next steps: send security pack, schedule POC benchmark, share prompt sets.

Topics: migration path, eval parity, dedicated capacity, private VPC, security/KMS, benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call, then we can jump into what you are trying to accomplish.
[00:18] Sam (Cedar Streams): Hey yeah, Sam here. Short on time so we wanted to get straight to how we move away from our current OpenAI-heavy flow and get more predictable costs for our realtime summarization and customer support routing.
[00:32] Alex: Great, and Maya on the line as well — she does most of the compatibility and infra questions. Maya?
[00:40] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick note: we've seen a lot of customers land like you by using Hosted while they prototype then shift to Dedicated or Private when they need consistent throughput and data controls.
[00:56] Priya (Cedar Streams): We're currently using a mix — OpenAI gpt-4x for high quality, and vLLM/TGI on-prem for some inference to cut cost. We're seeing output drift sometimes between the two, that's one of my big worries.
[01:12] Maya: Totally, parity is tricky. We do a two-track approach: model compatibility layer + eval harness. We'll pull your prompt corpus and run side-by-side comparisons — measure ngram overlap, semantic similarity, and specific business-critical metrics.
[01:32] Priya: And in terms of exact prompts, we have ~60 high-frequency prompts for routing and summarization. Latency budget is tight — p50 token generation needs to be under ~100ms when possible, end-to-end request under 350ms for certain paths.
[01:48] Evan (Infra): Also, we have a strict on-call & incident window. If you suggest Dedicated, we need to know failover plans, autoscale, and how bursting works. Can Redwood do burst to hosted if Dedicated is saturated?
[02:07] Alex: Yes — policy-based smart routing is built-in. You can prefer Dedicated for cost and SLO, and fallback to Hosted for bursts. We'll show that in the POC.
[02:18] Jordan (Security): Quick security note — we need SOC 2, KMS integration, customer HSM, and audit logs for requests. Any data residency implications? We run in us-west-2 primarily.
[02:34] Maya: We support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs in Private and Dedicated. Our Hosted product also supports encrypted at rest with bring-your-own-key options for certain enterprise tiers. We'll attach the security pack.
[02:51] Sam: Good. On the compatibility front, we run TGI for local workers and vLLM in some clusters; the behaviour difference vs OpenAI is causing us to tune prompts a lot. If we move to Redwood, what's the lift to keep parity?
[03:09] Maya: There are two parts: first, kernel/runtime behavior: Redwood's runtime has continuous batching, KV cache handling, and quantization paths. We can map model variants — e.g., if you use OpenAI’s 1.2B-ish family we can route to an equivalent open model with quantization to meet latency/cost. Second, the eval: we run A/Bs across prompt sets and produce deltas so you can accept/reject variants.
[03:35] Priya: Any docs about how you handle prefix caching and long-context tokens? For reranking we keep KV caches across sessions.
[03:44] Maya: Yes, we have caching docs; short answer is we keep KV cache warm and can pin sessions to reduce cold-start. We'll share the KB link after this meeting.
[03:58] [crosstalk] Priya: That would be great.
[04:05] Alex: On pricing, we typically show Hosted per-token, Dedicated committed capacity with reserved vGPU pools, and Private with enterprise licensing. For your volume can you say tokens/day?
[04:18] Priya: Right now single-digit millions; expected to grow to mid double-digit millions in 6 months. Cost target is roughly 30-40% below current OpenAI spend while keeping quality close.
[04:33] Alex: Makes sense — we'll prepare a TCO sketch.
[04:40] Sam: For the POC we'd like to validate both throughput and output parity. Can Redwood run our prompt set against both hosted and a dedicated pool with the same model family to compare?
[04:54] Maya: Yep — that's a standard POC. We'll benchmark p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and produce diffs on generated text. We'll annotate hallucination rates if you have ground truth.
[05:09] Jordan: On the compliance side, is there a way to keep logs for a year and have RBAC so only certain roles can retrieve full transcripts?
[05:21] Maya: Audit retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private. RBAC is supported via SSO and role mappings. We'll include the RBAC guide.
[05:34] Evan: During POC we'll need an infra runbook. If we test a 2-hour bench, what metrics do you need us to set up?
[05:45] Maya: Network egress metrics, load generator (we recommend Fortio/JMeter), and a consistent prompt load. We'll run with pinned seeds to get reproducible samples.
[05:58] Priya: One more thing — tokenization differences across runtimes have bitten us. What's Redwood's tokenizer compatibility layer?
[06:08] Maya: We support model-specific tokenizers plus a normalization layer. For example, we can replicate the exact BPE for model X or emulate OpenAI tokenization for parity checks. We'll surface a tokenizer diff report in the eval results.
[06:26] Sam: That helps. Also curious about quantized model performance — some of our internal tests with vLLM + 4-bit quantization improved cost but slightly changed semantics. What's the tradeoff with Redwood's quantization recommendations?
[06:42] Maya: We provide recommended quant profiles per workload. For many summarization tasks you can use 4-bit quant with minimal delta; for highly sensitive completions we recommend 8-bit or fp16. We'll include sample regression reports.
[06:58] Alex: Circling back to timeline — are you planning to make a decision quickly?
[07:05] Sam: We want to kick off a POC in the next two weeks if possible, decision within 4-6 weeks after a successful POC. Budget is approved for a pilot.
[07:15] Alex: Great. We'll turn around the pricing and security pack ASAP.
[07:21] [pause]
[07:30] Priya: Operational question — does Redwood provide per-route model pinning? For example, we want Route A to use a higher-quality model and Route B to use a cheaper quantized version.
[07:43] Maya: Yes, per-route configuration, rollout policies, and automatic fallback. You can pin by model version, quality profile, and even hardware class (e.g., A100 pool vs T4 pool).
[07:57] Evan: If Dedicated goes down for maintenance, what's our SLA and what's the default fallback?
[08:07] Maya: Enterprise Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and you can configure automatic fallback to Hosted in another region. We'll show failover time estimates in the runbook.
[08:20] Jordan: How are secrets handled? We need integration with our KMS and optional HSM-backed keys.
[08:29] Maya: We support BYOK via KMS and can work with HSM in Private deployments. We'll include integration notes and example policies.
[08:41] Sam: Ok, that's mostly my checklist. Anything else on the eval metrics?
[08:45] Maya: We'll also run cost-per-token breakdown, per-route latency and tail analysis, and a small set of business metrics you choose — e.g., summary correctness and routing accuracy.
[08:57] Priya: For the A/B comparisons, will you surface model diffs at the token-level or at a higher semantic metric?
[09:05] Maya: Both. Token-level diffs and semantic similarity scores (embedding cosine) plus human-labeled accept/reject where you provide ground truth.
[09:16] Alex: Quick recap: Redwood sends security pack + quant/compat checklist + Dedicated pricing; Cedar Streams shares prompt set and token volume; we schedule a 2-hour POC benchmark with infra. Is that correct?
[09:30] Sam: Yep, that's right.
[09:33] Alex: Any blockers on requiring Private instead of Dedicated?
[09:37] Jordan: If we can satisfy KMS, audit logs, and residency in our region, Dedicated might be fine; Private is preferred if we can't have BYOK in Hosted tiers. We'll decide after review.
[09:50] Alex: Perfect. We'll aim to get materials by Monday. Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Sam: Thanks.

Closing notes:
- Links to be shared: security pack (link sent after meeting), POC runbook (draft), tokenization guide, quantization recommendations.
- References mentioned in call: internal benchmark spreadsheet (will be attached), sample prompt corpus (customer to share).

End of transcript.
